pirate.definition: A person who uses another person's words or ideas as if they were their own.

princess.definition: A female member of a royal family other than the queen (especially the daughter of a sovereign).

knight.definition: Originally a person of noble birth trained to arms and chivalry.

wizard.definition: Possessing or using or characteristic of or appropriate to supernatural powers.

fairy.definition: A small being, human in form, playful and having magical powers.

cowboy.definition: A person who is reckless or irresponsible (especially in driving vehicles).

astronaut.definition: A person trained to travel in a spacecraft.

robot.definition: A mechanism that can move automatically.

superhero.definition: A fictional character with superhuman powers.

ninja.definition: A member of the ninja who were trained in martial arts and hired for espionage or sabotage or assassinations.

cat-ears.definition: A costume accessory shaped like a cat's ears and worn on the head.
cat-ears.exampleUsage: She wore cat ears with the animal costume.

bunny-tail.definition: A small round costume accessory designed to look like a rabbit's tail.
bunny-tail.exampleUsage: The bunny tail attached to the back of the costume.

lion-mane.definition: A costume piece designed to resemble the thick hair around a male lion's head and neck.
lion-mane.exampleUsage: The lion mane fitted around the child's hood.

dinosaur-suit.definition: A costume designed to make the wearer look like a dinosaur.
dinosaur-suit.exampleUsage: The dinosaur suit had a padded tail.

butterfly-wings.definition: Decorative costume wings shaped and colored like a butterfly's wings.
butterfly-wings.exampleUsage: The butterfly wings were attached with shoulder straps.

bear-onesie.definition: A one-piece costume or sleepwear item styled to look like a bear.
bear-onesie.exampleUsage: The bear onesie had small ears on the hood.

shark-fin.definition: A costume accessory shaped like the fin on a shark's back.
shark-fin.exampleUsage: A soft shark fin was attached to the costume.

ladybug.definition: A small red or black insect with spots on its back.
ladybug.exampleUsage: The ladybug was identified during the lesson.

frog-hat.definition: A hat designed with features that make it resemble a frog.
frog-hat.exampleUsage: The frog hat had large fabric eyes.

monkey-mask.definition: A face covering designed to resemble a monkey's face.
monkey-mask.exampleUsage: The monkey mask was made from soft costume material.

mask.definition: A covering to disguise or conceal the face.

wig.definition: Hairpiece covering the head and made of real or synthetic hair.

hat.definition: Headdress that protects the head from bad weather.

cape.definition: A strip of land projecting into a body of water.

sword.definition: A cutting or thrusting weapon that has a long metal blade and a hilt with a hand guard.
sword.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Sword" in an educational description.

shield.definition: Armor carried on the arm to intercept blows.

wand.definition: A rod used by a magician or water diviner.

crown.definition: The part of a hat (the vertex) that covers the crown of the head.

tiara.definition: A jeweled headdress worn by women on formal occasions.

eye-patch.definition: A small covering worn over one eye, either for medical reasons or as part of a costume.
eye-patch.exampleUsage: The pirate costume included a decorative eye patch.

face-paint-set.definition: A collection of skin-safe cosmetic paints and tools for creating temporary designs on the face.
face-paint-set.exampleUsage: The face-paint set included several washable colors.

makeup-brush.definition: A small brush designed for applying cosmetic products.
makeup-brush.exampleUsage: The makeup brush was cleaned after use.

glitter.definition: The quality of shining with a bright reflected light.

false-eyelashes.definition: Artificial lashes attached temporarily along the eyelid to make the eyelashes appear longer or fuller.
false-eyelashes.exampleUsage: The costume kit included reusable false eyelashes.

spirit-gum.definition: A sticky solution of gum and ether is used to attach artificial hair to the skin.

fake-blood.definition: A non-blood theatrical material made to look like blood for costumes, film, or stage effects.
fake-blood.exampleUsage: The costume used washable fake blood for a stage effect.

scar-wax.definition: A moldable theatrical makeup material used to create the appearance of scars or raised skin effects.
scar-wax.exampleUsage: The makeup artist shaped scar wax for a fictional character.

color-palette.definition: A physical palette or digital interface that lets artists and designers arrange, view, and choose colors for a project.

fabric-roll.definition: A long continuous length of fabric wound around a tube or core.
fabric-roll.exampleUsage: The shop stored each fabric roll on a shelf.

sequin.definition: Adornment consisting of a small piece of shiny material used to decorate clothing.

feather.definition: Branching, hair-like structure that grows on the bodies of birds.
feather.exampleUsage: The feather was identified during the lesson.

velvet.definition: A silky densely piled fabric with a plain back.

satin.definition: A smooth fabric of silk or rayon.

tulle.definition: A fine (often starched) net used for veils or tutus or gowns.

elastic.definition: A fabric made of yarns containing an elastic material.

zipper.definition: A fastener with two rows of teeth that join when a slider moves along them.

button.definition: Any artifact that resembles a button.

thread.definition: Any long object resembling a thin line.

mannequin.definition: A woman who wears clothes to display fashions.

display-rack.definition: A frame or stand used to hold and show products for customers to see.
display-rack.exampleUsage: Masks and hats hung on the display rack.

fitting-room.definition: A private room where customers can try on clothing or costumes.
fitting-room.exampleUsage: The customer tried the costume in the fitting room.

full-length-mirror.definition: A tall mirror large enough to show most or all of a standing person's body.
full-length-mirror.exampleUsage: A full-length mirror stood outside the fitting room.

price-tag.definition: A figurative price tag is the cost or result that comes with making a particular choice.

shopping-bag.definition: A bag made from plastic or durable paper, often with handles, carries purchased goods home from a shop.

shelf.definition: A support that consists of a horizontal surface for holding objects.

register.definition: A machine used to record sales and take payments in a shop.

catalog.definition: A book or pamphlet containing an enumeration of things.

tutu.definition: South African prelate and leader of the antiapartheid struggle (born in 1931).

armor.definition: Protective clothing made to shield a person in battle or performance.

gown.definition: The members of a university as distinguished from the other residents of the town in which the university is located.

wings.definition: A means of flight or ascent.

boots.definition: Compartment in an automobile that carries luggage or shopping or tools.
boots.exampleUsage: The boots was used during the activity.

gloves.definition: The handwear used by fielders in playing baseball.

belt.definition: An elongated region where a specific condition or characteristic is found.

fabric.definition: Artifact made by weaving or felting or knitting or crocheting natural or synthetic fibers.

ribbon.definition: Any long object resembling a thin line.

lace.definition: A delicate decorative fabric woven in an open web of symmetrical patterns.

silk.definition: A fabric made from the fine threads produced by certain insect larvae.
silk.exampleUsage: The silk was identified during the lesson.
